title: Dawson's claim to start picking the bass; other early bassists
summary: Dawson says he started four-four finger picking, which Pop Foster and others followed; remembers Jimmy Johnson and Jimmy Brown.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: That's right. A good bow. Do you remember, Sir Dorsey, the first time you heard anybody pick on the bass? Well, I was the first one started that, right down in the district.

I started Pop Foster, and he'll tell you he's living the day. I started with that one finger, picking that four-four rhythm. And from that on, they start making that four-four rhythm, you know, picking with one finger like that. You put the bow down. And they just went right on up. And when I looked around there, all the bass players was playing that four-four rhythm. Then they was making that vancing all the time, you see. They got so they was playing with three fingers and stuff.
And you remember some of the other bass players you've mentioned, three or four. Any of the other fellas real early that you heard?

No, not the old fellas, no. Do you remember Jimmy Johnson? Jimmy Johnson. Was he older than you, I guess? Oh, yes, yes. He was older than me, yes. He died. He was a good bass player, yes. And Jimmy Johnson. I love him. And Jimmy Brown, too, was another bass player. He was the greatest one. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
